summary: Iteration 44 — Frontend testing of two new Iron Rabbit / Restaurants Galore features on top of iter_43: (A) Meal Plan Templates (save/apply/delete a whole week; week-relative day_offset storage) and (B) Family Preference Nudge (loved-Heart / allergen-AlertTriangle / neutral-ChefHat icons + tooltip title attributes in the Meal Plan recipe picker with allergen-wins priority). Full flow exercised live via IndexedDB seeding + Playwright: all 15 target checks PASS. Zero console/page errors. Regression on iter_43 meal-plan controls (grid, prev/next/this-week, add/remove, build-shopping, clear-week, range label) still visible & interactive.

action_items: Non-blocking UX: after selecting a recipe from meal-plan-picker-<date>, the Radix Popover trigger stays in data-state='open' (aria-expanded='true') because addEntry() doesn't programmatically close the popover. This means a second click on the same meal-plan-add-<date> button TOGGLES the popover closed instead of opening a fresh one — end users adding two recipes to the same day may see the picker snap shut on their second click. Playwright had to wait for data-state='closed' or press Escape between selects. Recommend calling `setOpen(false)` (or wrapping Popover in controlled state with open={openDate===dateIso} and clearing it in addEntry) so the popover closes on select — matches user expectation and eliminates a subtle usability quirk.

Non-blocking cosmetic: When switching weeks after applying a template, the modal doesn't scroll/flash any confirmation on the target-week tiles — the toast is the only signal. Could briefly pulse the newly-added meal-plan-entry-<id> nodes for improved feedback.

Non-blocking: Template chip only shows an 'Apply' as the whole button — no explicit label. The delete X is opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100, so on touch devices with no hover the delete is unreachable. Consider making the delete tap-target always visible on `md:` (touch) or adding a long-press.

Non-blocking: The empty-hint copy 'Save a week you love, then apply it to any future week in one tap.' has no data-testid — fine for now, but if the empty-state ever needs to be asserted a testid like meal-plan-tpl-empty-hint would help.
critical_code_review_comments: classifyRecipeForFamily (RestaurantMealPlanModal.jsx L32-54) — allergen matches on hay = title + ingredients, so allergen priority takes both title and ingredients into account; loved matches title only. This is the documented behavior and matches the 'allergen wins' UI ternary at L331-343. Clean, memoized via familyHitsByRecipe useMemo.
saveMealPlanTemplate (restaurantsService.js L636-652) clamps day_offset to 0..6 with `Math.max(0, Math.min(6, e.day_offset | 0))` — good defensive coding; also drops entries without recipe_id.

applyMealPlanTemplate (L659-672) — computes target date from `new Date(weekStartIso + 'T00:00:00')` (local time) which pairs correctly with mondayOf(...) in the modal that uses local Date arithmetic. Consistent time-zone handling; no UTC/local drift observed in tests (Mon offset 0 stayed Mon, Wed offset 2 stayed Wed).

Save-as-template (RestaurantMealPlanModal.jsx L117-134) uses `Date.parse(iso + 'T00:00:00Z')` (UTC) to compute day_offset — this MIXES UTC (offset compute) with LOCAL (applyMealPlanTemplate uses local Date). For non-UTC users this could cause off-by-one weekday drift if the modal is opened around midnight local time. Current test in UTC-ish env passed, but recommend making both sides use the same convention (either both UTC by suffixing 'T00:00:00Z', or both local). Not blocking today but a lurking timezone bug for global users.
Popover in the picker is uncontrolled (no `open` prop) — see action_items above regarding the same-day double-add UX quirk.
Template chip's delete uses window.confirm — consistent with existing Clear-week pattern in this file. Fine.
meal_plan_tpl is properly included in exportAll (L822), importAll (L904), and computeBackupDiff (L1008) — future-proof for backup/restore.
seed_data_creation: Via IndexedDB DB 'IronRabbit'. Opened Meal Plan modal once to lazily create rg_* object stores, then wrote via raw IDB: rg_restaurants['TEST_REST_1']={name:'TEST Bistro'}; rg_recipes['REC_A']={title:'Simple Pasta', ingredients:['pasta','olive oil','salt']}; rg_recipes['REC_B']={title:'Peanut Chicken', ingredients:['peanut butter','chicken']}; rg_recipes['REC_C']={title:'Grilled Salmon', ingredients:['salmon','lemon']}; rg_recipes['REC_D']={title:'Peanut Pasta', ingredients:['peanut butter','pasta']} (used for the both-hit priority test); rg_family['FAM_1']={name:'Test Kid', loved_dishes:['pasta'], allergies:['peanut']}. Cleared rg_meal_plan and rg_meal_plan_tpl between phases. Note: after writing to rg_* stores you MUST close and reopen the modal to see the changes since reload() only fires on isOpen transition.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two important gotchas: (1) Radix Popover in RestaurantMealPlanModal.jsx picker is uncontrolled and does NOT auto-close on select — so any script that adds multiple recipes to the same date must wait for aria-expanded='closed' on the meal-plan-add-<date> button (or press Escape) between selects, else the second add-button click toggles the still-open popover CLOSED. (2) The RG localforage instance uses DB name 'IronRabbit' and storeName 'rg_<name>' (e.g. 'rg_meal_plan_tpl'). Stores are created lazily, so open the Meal Plan modal once before writing to rg_meal_plan_tpl or rg_family via raw IDB, then close and reopen so the modal's reload() picks up your seed. Confirm/window.confirm dialogs are used for Clear-week and Delete-template — attach page.on('dialog', d.accept) before those clicks.
